findings.title: Connection: close cancels a run
findings.red_test: server::tests::a_program_answers_a_request_that_closes_its_connection (real serve loop over mutual TLS; the test plays code mode's helper and worker)
findings.red: 01-red-unmodified.log: CONNECTION_CLOSE program=1 program_frame_read=false worker_done_written=false client_read=Ok(0) answer_bytes=0 stops=[1]; panicked: no answer to the program's request: ""
findings.fix: server.rs: Conn.waiting is Option<(u64, AfterAnswer)>, AfterAnswer {Read, Close}. A deferred (Reply::Later) request that said Connection: close records AfterAnswer::Close instead of closing; serve sends close_notify right after writing that program's answer (or its cancellation answer). RFC 9112 section 9.6.

mutations.M1b (no close after the answer): killed: client_read=Err(WouldBlock) after 5 s, the connection not closed (17, 06a)

findings.unchanged: A client that ends its TLS stream or socket (EOF/error) while its program runs still cancels the program: the existing 'connection gone' rule.

findings.title: A lost STOP leaves a worker running
findings.red: 01-red-unmodified.log: LOST_STOP_DEADLINE program=1 control_messages_filling=278 drained=278 stops=[] answered_ended=true and LOST_STOP_GONE ... stops=[] (the instance answered 'was ended' with no STOP ever reaching the helper)
findings.fix: server.rs: Programs.unstopped, an owned set of STOPs the full control socket refused (WouldBlock); serve polls the control socket for POLLOUT while it is non-empty and sends them as it has room (Programs::send_stops). Its capacity is reserved at admission beside cancelled (one place per live program; a program is let go of once), so the push never allocates. The connection-gone path now stops only a program still running, and removes it, sends or queues its STOP, then drops its socket, as the deadline/failure and rpc-cancel paths already did.

mutations.M2 (WouldBlock dropped as before): killed by both tests, 3 of 3 rounds on the reordered source (10) and again on the committed source (17); on an intermediate source (09) only the deadline test killed it, which led to the reorder

findings.remaining_gap: A STOP refused for another cause (ENOBUFS, EPIPE) is still let go of, as before. EPIPE means the helper is gone and its workers with it (PR_SET_PDEATHSIG); ENOBUFS was not reproduced and is not addressed.

findings.title: hand allocates and zero-fills about 208 KiB every time
findings.red_test: broker::tests::a_small_hand_reserves_what_its_file_holds (real SEQPACKET peer, its limit read as the instance reads it: SO_SNDBUF - 32)
findings.red: 01-red-unmodified.log: HAND_RESERVATION channel_most=212960 file_bytes=10 packet_len=26 reserved_at_admission=212961 capacity_after_read=212961
findings.fix: broker.rs: reserve() holds a hand's head only (kind, ID, name length, name: Hand.head); Hand::read reserves after fstat for the file's size plus the probe byte, reads into the vector's spare capacity with read(2) (no zero-fill), and, if the file proves longer than its size said yet within the limit, widens to the old limit-plus-probe and reads on, so the size limit and probe semantics are as before.
findings.semantics_guard: broker::tests::a_file_longer_than_its_size_says_is_handed_as_before: /proc/self/status (fstat size 0) handed whole within the limit and refused TooLong past a 16-byte limit; passes before and after the fix

mutations.M4b (no widening when longer than its si: killed: the procfs file refused TooLong (17, 06b)

findings.not_measured: Allocation counts, page faults and time (R14, coordinator-owned). The zero-fill is gone by construction (no resize); only capacity was observed.

findings.title: Programs lose the typed broker result
findings.red_test: sandbox::tests::a_programs_broker_results_keep_their_receipt (QuickJS program, the instance played by the test)
findings.red: 02-red-optional-unmodified.log: BROKER_RECEIPT thrown=Ok("[\"agent a may not send agent c requests\",null]")
findings.fix: sandbox.rs PRELUDE: a reply's broker receipt is the thrown Error's cause (ES2022 Error cause) and a non-enumerable broker property of the returned value, so the value's JSON stays as declared; server.rs: the run tool's description says so.

findings.title: One failed reap ends the whole helper
findings.red_test: sandbox::tests::a_worker_not_reaped_ends_no_other (forks the test process to run the real helper loop with SIGCHLD ignored, so the kernel reaps workers and waitid fails with ECHILD; the failure text comes back over a pipe)
findings.red: 02-red-optional-unmodified.log: REAP_UNKNOWN first=[] control_closed=true worker_two_ran_on=false ... helper_code=3 helper_failure="reaping a worker: Uncategorized, OS Some(10); 2 workers not known reaped, first 2: ..."
findings.fix: sandbox.rs: a worker whose pidfd says it ended but whose status waitid does not give is reported in ENDED as END_UNKNOWN (code 0, status the errno) and untracked, and the helper serves on; server.rs worker_end renders END_UNKNOWN as 'how is not known (waitid: OS n)'. END_UNKNOWN = 0 lies outside waitid's CLD_* codes (1-6, include/uapi/asm-generic/siginfo.h) and apart from creation refusal's -1.

mutations.M6 (fatal reap restored): killed: helper_code=3, the other worker ended with it (17, 06c)

test_only_change_outside_the_findings.what: sandbox::tests::a_worker_is_ended_for_a_call_its_filter_refuses: its forked children call prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0) before they confine themselves.
test_only_change_outside_the_findings.why: On this runner (core_pattern |systemd-coredump, ulimit -c unlimited) its SIGSYS children each dumped a core; a dumping task keeps every descriptor it inherited from the multithreaded test process for the seconds the dump takes, so a socket another test closed stayed open. Observed: 398 SIGSYS cores of the test binary in 90 minutes; one failure of the existing test a_refused_native_release_does_not_reuse_its_issued_identity (10); the new fork test's own worker also dumped (a debug build's OwnedFd check calls fcntl, which the worker filter refuses), which the same prctl in that test's forked helper removes.
test_only_change_outside_the_findings.result: before: 3 failures in 104 whole-suite runs and 2-3 cores per run (12); with the existing test's prctl alone: 0 of 40, 1 core per run (13); with both: 0 of 60, 0 cores (14).
test_only_change_outside_the_findings.coordinator_decision: It edits an existing test the findings did not name; drop it if unwanted (the new fork test's own prctl suffices for its stability; the existing test's hazard then remains).

observation_not_fixed: In debug builds of production code, a worker dies by SIGSYS when it drops an OwnedFd: std's debug_assert_fd_is_open calls fcntl(2), which worker_calls() does not allow (core stack in 13). Release builds (guest profile, test-release) compile that check out; not reproduced in a production configuration, so not changed (R09).

rules.R01: No new panic paths in production: checked arithmetic or saturating_sub, try_reserve_exact, read(2) into spare capacity with set_len only of what read returned (both unsafe blocks documented). unstopped.push and cancelled.push rely on capacity reserved at admission, as running.push already did. clippy -D warnings clean on gnu and musl.
rules.R02: Specs cited: RFC 9112 section 9.6 (close after the response), waitid CLD_* codes (siginfo.h), ES2022 Error cause; kernel unix_dgram_poll writability for POLLOUT (wmem at most sndbuf/4).
rules.R03: One production literal: END_UNKNOWN = 0 (derivation above). Test waits (5 s, 300 ms, 1 s, 500 ms deadline) are fixtures only.
rules.R04: Typed states: AfterAnswer {Read, Close}; the unstopped set; END_UNKNOWN on the ENDED wire, rendered by worker_end; refusal literal kept apart from the uncertain literal.
rules.R05: POLLOUT readiness drives STOP retries (no periodic probe); no cache added.
rules.R06/R07/R13: Focused diffs at the existing seams; comments carry only rationale and sources.
rules.R08/R14: Not applicable to an implementer: no benchmark or profile run. Capacity values come from unit-test output.
rules.R09/R10: Red on unmodified code, then green, then each guard removed (9 mutants) and the fix restored, for all six findings, with logs in this directory.
rules.R11: shards-server is Linux-only. x86_64 gnu tested, x86_64 musl checked and linted. aarch64 Linux (gnu and musl) not built: unverified. macOS and Windows build only the stub main, unchanged and not built here.
rules.R15: Implementer, light tests only: no VM E2E, benchmarks or profiling. About 224 whole-suite runs of the light unit suite were made to find and fix a flake in the new tests (11-14), with no VMs.
rules.R16: Runner: about 440 SIGSYS cores (about 100 MB) of the test binary from these runs sit in /var/lib/systemd/coredump (root-owned, systemd vacuums them; not deleted). Debug target dirs for x86_64 gnu and musl remain in the runner's synced copy, regenerable and kept for reuse.
